name: The law & the covenants
about: What the law is for, and the covenants of God.

teachings.title: Usury and the Lord's release
teachings.summary: In the King James Bible usury is any interest on a loan, and God's law of the seventh-year release, the jubilee and no usury to the poor kept the needy from bondage, picturing redemption in Christ.
teachings.text:
Verse 8 cautions against usury and unjust gain, linking the two. Much is made about what the Bible means by usury. Some suggest that a little interest for a loan is fine, that it's just prohibited to charge high or "predatory" interest rates.

But, in the King James Bible, usury is defined as any interest, profit, or premium charged on a loan, not just excessive or illegal interest as understood in modern terms. When servitude could be the result of not keeping the terms of the agreement, compounding interest on top of the principle could be the difference between slavery or liberty. Seeking to profit off another's need is unjust gain.

Redemption is the freeing of the burden of debt, paying what's owed and liberating oneself or another from owing something. The gospel language of Christ setting us at liberty from the wages of sin through the gift of eternal life, where the Spirit acts as the surety for the promise of God, that He will not impute our sins against us, but rather apply the payment of Jesus' blood, is all quite deliberate.

So the idea of adding burdens to the needy that make their ability to pay someone back fairly is an abomination to the Lord. He is gracious and expects us to be gracious as well.

God's law instituted a "Sabbath year." Every seven years, a "release" was mandated, where creditors were required to cancel debts owed by their fellow Israelites.

**Deuteronomy 15:1-2**
*At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release. And this is the manner of the release: Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the Lord's release.*

Servitude could often be a means of survival for the poor, and a blessing. Having a way to work off that which is owed, without interest was a fair system, and limiting the debt to what could be repaid in 7 years not only kept this process from exploiting the poor, but made lenders more cautious in issuing loans.

But some have an evil heart, and their love of money tempts them. And so the Lord warns;

**Deuteronomy 15:9**
*Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto the Lord against thee, and it be sin unto thee.*

Not all debt was for money. Some servitude was to obtain favor or other gain.

In **Genesis 29**, Laban tricks Jacob into a total of 14 years of labor for the honor of marriage to Rachel, Laban's younger daughter. After Jacob serves seven years, Laban switches his daughters on the wedding night, sending his older daughter, Leah, to the bridal bed instead of Rachel. Laban justifies this deceit by claiming it is custom for the younger to marry after the older, but he sought to keep Jacob bound to service, exploiting his love for Rachel.

In addition to the 7 year release, God commands a jubilee every 50 years;

**Leviticus 25:10-13**
*And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family. A jubile shall that fiftieth year be unto you: ye shall not sow, neither reap that which groweth of itself in it, nor gather the grapes in it of thy vine undressed. For it is the jubile; it shall be holy unto you: ye shall eat the increase thereof out of the field. In the year of this jubile ye shall return every man unto his possession.*

The purpose here was to restore families to their land, and set free the captive, that generational poverty could be prevented. Stopping a lending class of rich men from exerting permanent control over the poor.

If lending to a poor neighbor, one was forbidden from charging usury at all;

**Exodus 22:25**
*If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer, neither shalt thou lay upon him usury.*

teachings.title: Nations seeking the Jew fulfilled in Christ
teachings.summary: The promise that nations would seek God with the Jews failed through their blindness and is fulfilled in Christ, with salvation by Jesus rather than by the nation.
teachings.text:
Just as the men had asked about the fasting they'd taken up by tradition in exile, the Lord lists all such fasts that they do, and says instead these shall be feasts in Jerusalem if they love the truth and peace.

And He promises that if they do these things, it shall come to pass that there shall come people, from all nations and tongues to pray to the Lord in Jerusalem. Even grabbing the hem of the Jew, saying they will go with the , for they have heard that God is with them.

Another promise where the Jews fell short to achieve, but that is fulfilled in Christ.

They were to be a light unto the Gentiles, to be teachers of the word. Instead they were blind guides, and taught for commandments the doctrines of men. Unable to bring forth fruit. Hypocrites and vipers.

So, instead of salvation being of the Jews, as the prophets said, it was by Jesus from the Jews. The promised Kingdom of God delayed, and for His people who believe on Christ, rather than the nation which had all the advantages. Even the oracles of God.

teachings.title: Salvation by faith, national promises by works
teachings.summary: Individual salvation was always by grace through faith, but God's national promises to Israel were conditional on their obedience, and they failed and were cast out.
teachings.text:
While spiritual salvation was always by grace through faith for individuals, without any other conditions, the national promises were always contingent on works.

Separation, sacrifice and ritual cleansing to maintain the presence of the glory of God, which we saw earlier in Ezekiel, went out from the Temple, and here in these prophecies, promised to return, if they got right. And the Law was perfect and glorious to that end. The fault wasn't with that covenant, but with the people.

**Hebrews 8:6-8**
*But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah*

The moral law and commandments, which are still in effect today in the NT, were a schoolmaster to lead us to Christ for salvation. Same then as today. Even the law written in our hearts, for the Gentiles without the advantage of the oracles of God. All have sinned and fallen short, so we need a spiritual redeemer.

But the laws of sanctification and reconciliation for the physical nation were not only doable, but God gave pretty explicit instructions on how to maintain it, which some of the time -  during the period of the Wilderness, the entry into the promised land, here and there during the time of Judges and Kings, they managed to keep. And had God's blessings upon them.

Israel was meant to be a light unto the world. Showing all nations that if they did these things and sought after God, they would be blessed as well. Eventually, it would lead to the culmination of the time of Christ, the BRANCH, The Lord, the King of Kings, coming to establish all of the end times promises of the Kingdom given to the people. In the city He chose to place His name. In the line of David as promised.

And they would not.

So, when Jesus did come, the leaders of the Jews were unable to deliver a people meet for repentance. They, being teachers of the Law were blind guides, thinking that whatever promises they had, were deserved being "Abraham's seed." That their added rituals and Pharisaical cleansings meant they deserved both the spiritual salvation and the restoration of their earthly kingdom.

And rather than being ready for the Kingdom, they were instead cut off and cast out.

**Matthew 8:11-12**
*And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.*

teachings.title: Promises withdrawn when the people fail
teachings.summary: With the priesthood changed the law changed, and like Saul and others, Israel lost conditional end-times promises by their own unbelief without making God a liar.
teachings.text:
This is why they expected a conquering Christ and an earthly kingdom. This is why they placed more value in the carnal and forgot the spiritual things of God, like mercy and judgment. Their entitled attitudes, after so long a period of judgment and chastisement against Israel by God to get them to get right, was the result of hardened hearts and stuff necks.

And so they killed Christ and His death and blood entered us into a new testament, a better covenant. With better promises. Not a physical nation of the law and circumcision of the flesh, but a spiritual nation and a people circumcised of the heart.

And with the fading away of the Mosaic covenant, there was a necessary change made to the law.

**Hebrews 7:12**
*For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.*

The end to the Levitical priesthood of Aaron or Zadok, an end to sacrifices and diverse washings and Sabbaths and carnal ordinances. All these things satisfied in Jesus.

But the end of the Old Testament also meant the elimination of certain aspects of the end times prophecies. Not all, but some.

Just as the children of Israel who left Egypt and were promised Canaan, yet died in the wilderness, just as Saul was given **two** chances to be part of the lineage of Christ (once from his own anointment, and a second chance through his daughter Mical and David), just as all the other people who had a promise made that they lost by their own actions.

**1 Samuel 13:13-14**
*And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever. But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the Lord hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the Lord commanded thee.*

Just as David would have built the first Temple, but his actions ended that, and Solomon built it instead.

These missed opportunities didn't make God a liar when He promised them. But He rightly withdrew them when those the promises were made to didn't keep up their end.

teachings.title: Compromisers and the old paths
teachings.summary: Those who call standards legalism repeat Israel's compromise, and God eventually gives such people up to their delusions.
teachings.text:
With all the talk about "legalism" and preaching against standards, and calling "the old paths" divisive, you have to wonder if the compromisers actually read chapters like Ezekiel 20.

The children of Israel continually left His statutes, and His judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them - old paths that He gave them, that they might know that He is the Lord that sanctified them.

They compromised. They said to themselves "Why offer at the temple? We have high places. We can give our sweet savor to this idol in His name. We can keep our own sabbaths, not His." And so each generation filled themselves up with the measure of their fathers, and rejected more and more the path of the Lord.

The people compromising today, claiming to be doing the will of God by telling people to not worry about keeping the law, that it be well with them. To not have moral standards and behavior. They are a stubborn and rebellious people.

And you'll note that God eventually will give them up to their own delusions. To allow them to go on down the road to perdition. If they don't hear His voice and see the value in His statutes, then He eventually will leave them to wallow in that mire. To return to their vomit. And the firey flames will consume them.

teachings.title: The law given for our good
teachings.summary: God's statutes are given for our good, that it be well with us, and pastors who call the law grievous sound like Satan in the garden.
teachings.text:
Something I have posted about frequently, but bears repeating again in the context of the prophets, and even here in **Ezekiel 20**, notice that the commandments of God, His statutes and judgments aren't held over the people as punishment or "just because I say so," but that it be well with us, that we dwell long in the land, that it is a sign unto us that we are His people and He is our Lord. That we may know He is God. It's always given as a positive thing for us. Wisdom. Knowledge. All come from fear of the Lord and to the best of our fleshly abilities, walking in His judgment. The old paths. Neither turning to the Left or the Right.

People claiming to be saved Christians who still see the law as something grievous, as something we don't need, well they sound like Satan in the garden. A murderer from the first. Who hated Adam and Eve, and wanted them to fall and die just as he was condemned himself.

Shame on saved pastors denying the blessing of the law to their flock.

teachings.title: The true purpose of God's commandments
teachings.summary: Beyond being a schoolmaster and for the lawless, the law's real purpose is to show the saved God's will for a successful life, not to earn salvation.
teachings.text:
*Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper withersoever thou goest. This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success. Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.*

This is the true purpose of God's commandments. This is how the law is relevant to those saved by the law of liberty, by grace through faith in Christ Jesus.

Yes the law is a schoolmaster that brings us to understand we need salvation. Yes the law of for the lawless, that they may be punished according to the will and perfect judgement of God.

But it's real purpose is for a righteous people to know the will of God for their lives, and in keeping it as best they can, have a prosperous and successful life in service to our God.

Those that make this obedience to the law their gospel, and seek to work their own righteousness as a means of achieving or maintaining their salvation, miss the point and whatever gain they receive is offset by their constant doubts and fears. Not having faith, they please not God. Their filthy rags of their own righteousness give them nothing but hopelessness.

This isn't a prosperity gospel. There is no promise of riches and earthly wealth. But true success in our walk with Christ. Being taken care of, all we need, that we may store up riches in heaven. That we may be saved and all our house. That we may win souls and edify the brethren.

Amen

teachings.title: Lend not upon usury to thy brother
teachings.summary: He teaches believers should back a brother in need or enterprise without interest, within a jubilee limit, while noting the stranger clause has been abused.
teachings.text:
*Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury; but unto thy brother thou shalt not lend upon usury: that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all that thou settest thine hand to in the land whither thou goest to possess it.*

This one has been used as a loophole to justify the antichrists being allowed usury among Gentiles and Christians for centuries, and we are all aware of how that ends up.

The spirit of this for us today is that we should, as some communities do, practice the idea of investing and backing a brother in creative enterprise or in need, without taking advantage of the desperate or drawing interest from them, profiting from what might be a bad situation. Allowing the borrower a chance to repay without compounding the amount. Understanding this is in conjunction with the 7th year being a jubilee, therefore not loaning more than could be paid back in 6yrs of labor.

If only we had such a system here.

teachings.title: The law protected marriage and virginity
teachings.summary: He explains the laws on virginity, adultery, rape and fornication as perfect law that protected women and men and deterred immorality.
teachings.text:
Continuing **Deuteronomy 22**, God provides a provision for keeping the honor of a woman of she be taken in marriage, and known by a man who decides he doesn't want her, and uses a false accusation of lying about her virginity to put her away.

The parents have a right to bring the tokens of her virginity, the bloody bedding from the breaking of her hymen, and have him fined a substantial sum, to restore their honor. But if she's found lying, and was indeed deflowered, she was to be stoned.

We see that this was Joseph's dilemma betrothed to his wife Mary, having not consummated the marriage, and she being with child. He did the honorable thing to save her reputation (and had they not been under Roman law, her life).

Adulterers are put to death. It is evil to take another man's wife.

Fornication in a populated area is not considered rape, because the woman had opportunity to summon others to help her. Had it been rape, the rapist would be put to death, she would be as innocent as a victim of murder would. It is assumed she's a victim of rape if it occurs out in the field, where no witnesses could have come to her aid. This applies to betrothed virgins. Essentially a fornication that is worse than adultery.

A virgin, not betrothed, caught in fornication would then be married to her paramour. A dowery paid to the father.

These rules were to maintain order, avoid innocent bloodshed, keep honor in Israel and deter fornication. It is far better than where we find ourselves. Feminists hate it, and even supposed conservative Christians are offended by these things. But the law of God is perfect. It protected women and men, and deterred behavior that leads to the immoral state we find ourselves in today.

The last verse, against incest with a step-mother, is self-explanatory.

teachings.title: No dispensation, no repeal
teachings.summary: He teaches God's civil laws still stand for nations, the law being a schoolmaster to bring men to Christ, because God and His judgment on the wicked do not change.
teachings.text:
As we head into the civil laws God gave us, those still in effect. Not the carnal ordinances and meats and diverse washings of the Levitical laws, which were a picture of Christ, but the nitty-gritty administration of a godly nation, keep in mind that these prohibitions and directives stand today. These are things a nation that wishes to live long in their land and be fruitful, should adhere to.

There is no dispensation, there is no repeal.

**1 Timothy 1:8-11**
*But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, for whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; according to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

Those that say "that was then, now we are in the Gospel of Grace, and so we shouldn't care about the law" fail to understand that we are called to execute His judgements. And they serve a purpose; acting as a schoolmaster, bringing others to Christ.

**Galatians 3:24-27**
*Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*

They deny the opportunity for the wrath of God and His judgement from revealing His will from heaven and bringing those who have not believed to understanding. In fact, the more lawless a society, the less faith in God there is among the people. More victims of degenerates and reprobates. More temptations for the unregenerate to be snared in. It allows for a rod for God to scourge even His sons who backslide. That the sword isn't used in vain.

God doesn't change. Jesus is God, and thought the gospel of Christ has brought many to liberty, His judgment on the wicked isn't changed at all.

*Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.* Amen.

teachings.title: Release of debts a picture of salvation
teachings.summary: The release of servants and debts in the seventh year pictures salvation in Christ, so we should forgive debts as God forgave ours and send others away blessed.
teachings.text:
I covered the law of jubilee before, in [Leviticus 25](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/11512). It is worth noting again that the redemption of the servant and the forgiveness of debts, like the Hebrews being freed from bondage in Egypt, are pictures of the salvation found in Christ Jesus. We are called upon to release people of their obligation to us, in time. That if they haven't paid us back by the 7th year, to forgive them their debt, as God has forgiven ours.

*And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee: therefore I command thee this thing to day.*

And as a servant, not just sent away at the end of the term, but sent away with blessings and furnished to succeed on their own. Not as you took them in, but *wherewith the Lord thy God hath blessed thee thou shalt give unto him.*

Just as God does every believer.

Think not too highly of yourself. Remember your fallen state. Remember that God has sealed you as the servant who will not leave your side. As the pierced ear signified here in the law. We are sealed by the Spirit, to be His servants forever.

teachings.title: His commandments come with a promise
teachings.summary: He teaches that God forgives His children in Christ and gives commandments only so that it be well with us, wanting to bless us and train us as princes of His Kingdom.
teachings.text:
One of the reasons for the forgiveness of God the Father through the Son is to prove to His adopted children that He loves us unconditionally. That He's not judging our mistakes, forgiven in Christ, and wants to reward those who diligently seek Him. He just wants to bless us with the best life possible in this fallen world. His Commandments are always given with the promise that we'd prosper if we heed them. That we'd live long on the earth. "That it be well with you." He really just wants to share creation with you and build up judgment and grace, charity and love, to be just princes in the Kingdom. To understand how to be servants, first. To be fruitful and multiply. To have a homeland. Peace.

It's all God wants for us. It's foolish to think you can do better doing it your way.

teachings.title: Love God and thy neighbour, for thy good
teachings.summary: He teaches the God of the Old Testament is the same as the New, that His commandments were always for our good, and that making them a means of salvation breeds selfishness.
teachings.text:
There is a mistaken idea that the God of the Old Testament is somehow different from the New. That Jesus replaces wrath with "love." But it is this kindness, love towards others, that comes from loving God and keeping His ways, that has always been the point. Love God and love thy neighbour, that it be well with you. For your good.

We are at liberty in Christ, this leads to blessings, which leads to richness and bounty. And as God repeatedly warns the Israelites before going to the promised land, don't forget that's where your richness originated. That it is God's mercy and love that blessed us, so that we might share those blessings with the less fortunate, and deliver them from the wicked. It is the entire point of the gospel. Not simply our salvation, but that we get the opportunity to be servants of God, ministering to others. Edifying the brethren. Building His church by winning souls. Converting others by our good conversation, our behavior. With meekness and humility. Longsuffering and patience.

Christianity is a religion of low-time preference. Delayed gratification. And these qualities, as even the secular people know, compounds blessings on those who are able to have them. That it be well with us.

People who make the commandments of God into the means by which they are saved, become impulsive and selfish. Judgmental instead of rightly judging. They develop high-time preference, because they aren't doing good out of love and respect for God and the mercy He has shown us, but to save their own skin and prove how righteous they are. Selfish. And over time that compounds to a fallen nation. A loss of the blessings of liberty. Ultimately the destruction of the people, who turn from God and resent their neighbors and the stranger. Neglecting the fatherless and the widow. Rising up to play.

**Revelation 3:17**
*Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked*...

**Deuteronomy 8:11-14**
*Beware that thou forget not the Lord thy God, in not keeping his commandments, and his judgments, and his statutes, which I command thee this day: Lest when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and dwelt therein; And when thy herds and thy flocks multiply, and thy silver and thy gold is multiplied, and all that thou hast is multiplied; Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the Lord thy God, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage*

teachings.title: The commandments are still in force
teachings.summary: He refutes professing Christians who use the end of ceremonial laws to excuse sodomy and adultery, teaching that God's moral commandments still stand.
teachings.text:
*Thou shalt not kill.*

*Neither shalt thou commit adultery.*

*Neither shalt thou steal.*

*Neither shalt thou bear false witness against thy neighbour.*

*Neither shalt thou desire thy neighbour's wife, neither shalt thou covet thy neighbour's house, his field, or his manservant, or his maidservant, his ox, or his ass, or any thing that is thy neighbour's*

The 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th commandments as God gave them, are simple to understand, and as eternally relevant as the first five.

There are some professing Christians today who claim the civil laws of God and His commandments given Moses, are no longer in force. They point to the ceremonial laws and carnal ordinances of the Levitical priesthood that were done away with in Christ, and apply it to things like sodomy and adultery. Saying that these things are allowed in the New Testament. That the death penalty has been done away with. That God now loves abominations. "If the dietary laws aren't in effect, if you can eat pork and shrimp, then there's nothing wrong with being a Sodomite!"

Of course, these same people would not claim that murder, cheating on a spouse, stealing, perjuring or coveting the things of others are now ok.

They simply want to call evil good and good evil. They want to pick and choose, and not knowing scripture or hoping those they seek to mislead don't, they make these ridiculous claims.

But we know better.

*Ye shall observe to do therefore as the Lord your God hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left. Ye shall walk in all the ways which the Lord your God hath commanded you, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days in the land which ye shall possess.*

teachings.title: The jubilee pictures Christ's redemption
teachings.summary: The sabbatical years and jubilee picture Christ as near kinsman redeemer, with the trumpet of jubilee pointing to His second coming and our redemption.
teachings.text:
Leviticus chapter 25 brings us the law of Jubilee, a perpetual sabbatical observation of the 7th year, in the land of Canaan which the Lord brought the children of Israel, culminating in the 49th year, 7 times 7, a jubilee, a proclamation of liberty, wherein all God's children shall be redeemed.

Of course this parallels with Christ, and the redemption from the bonds of sin He makes for us, as the near kin, the Son of man, setting us free.

The particulars of this law, which wouldn't take effect for the Isralites until they had settled the land, driving out the former inhabitants and dividing by lot the tribes and the habitations thereof, showed not only the foresight of God's providence, but His terms as the actual owner, the land Lord so to speak, of the land He gives them.

And so, 6 years the fields are sown and the vineyards dressed, but in the 7th, there was no work to be done in the land. God promises them that the 6th year will be bountiful enough to tide them over to the 9th year, that they could live off their stores, because God provides all. Not of their own works.

The timing of the jubilee, which was marked in the 49th year, 7 sabbaths, was marked at the end of the fall feasts by the trumpets at the end of the day of atonement.

Just as Pentecost is celebrating the 7th sabbath after Passover, the spring feasts, represent Christs work here at His first coming, then the Jubilee is marked by the fall feast, which is emblematic of His second, and the day of redemption for believers. The trumpet sounds to announce the victory of the Lord, the atonement bought with blood, the redemption from bondage and the liberty given all, rich or poor.

teachings.title: Woe to them that join house to house
teachings.summary: God's jubilee law forbade usury and the hoarding of land, a fair system neither capitalist nor communist that kept families and tribes intact and still shows how to live.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 5:8**
*Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!*

God hates unfair dealings, taking advantage of others for profit, especially in their poverty. Unjust weights and measures. Mistreatment of servants. Usury among His people and the accumulation of property and capital, to the exclusion of others.

Basically, Capitalism.

But that is not to say He endorsed Communism, either. But fair and righteous trade and checks on over accumulation of wealth, or subjugation of His people. Productive enterprise and free markets (little f, little m), were the way He provided.

This system was fair and just and kept in remembrance of God being who we rely on, who provides for all. Rich or poor, servant or free.

The right of return to their own place, the inheritance they claim, enabled the genealogies to be recorded, and kept the tribes separated as He had ordained through the lots when it was eventually divided.

It kept the integrity of nations, as a people, as kin.

The genealogies also then served a purpose, bringing us to Christ's human family being perfect in its generations as it is given in the Gospel. And the real jubilee being the ultimate sabbath, which is Jesus.

The elegance and perfection of this law shouldn't be lost in the allegory or spiritual application, however. It really is the way that we should live, even today.

teachings.title: Choose life: Christ the end of the law
teachings.summary: He teaches the law set life and death before Israel, its righteousness proving the need for the righteousness of faith, for Christ is the end of the law to all who believe.
teachings.text:
Following the blessings promised and the cursings threatened by the Lord against the people of Israel in the Mosaic covenant, God makes clear it is their choice. A free will gesture, to either choose life or choose death.

And because of the fault of the people, the law became a ministration of death.

He says to them that they have the oracles of God before them. They don't need someone to go up into Heaven and return with them, they are right there. They do not need someone to go over the sea, or descend to its depths as Paul rephrases it, the Law is before them. Their love of God and faith of the heart determines if they are willing to seek life or choose death.

The word is very nigh unto them, even in their mouth. Even in their hearts. That the righteousness of the law may prove the need for the righteousness of faith and the grace and mercy of God.

*For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth. For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them.*

teachings.title: Why the law cannot save
teachings.summary: Keeping God's law is for our good but not for salvation, since no one can keep it all; the law is a schoolmaster bringing us to Christ to be justified freely by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
We should also remember that obedience to the civil laws of God are for our benefit. For our good always. That it be well with us. That it prolongs our days and that we are preserved alive. Not for salvation. Not for our own righteousness.

The law is a schoolmaster, teaching us our need for salvation in Christ.

**Galatians 3:24-27**
*Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*

Because;

I*t shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.*

If we observed to do **all** these commandments, it would be our righteousness. We would have to glory.

**Romans 4:1-12**
*What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, And whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also: and the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.*

But knowing that it is impossible in our flesh to observe all these things, we understand that it is God's glory that His mercy is revealed.

**James 2:10**
*For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.*

**Romans 3:10-12**
*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.*
*They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.*

As Paul writes a few verses later, *There is no fear of God before their eyes.* But as Moses writes here in **Deuteronomy 6**, under the same Spirit as Paul, we are to learn the law of God and keep it in our hearts, in our minds, *That thou mightest fear the Lord thy God*.

And in that fear, that respect and love of the Lord, we may know we have His mercy towards us:

**Romans 3:23-26**
*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.*

teachings.title: The law annulled as by a husband's death
teachings.summary: The law is the ministry of death made null by Christ's death as a marriage ends at a husband's death, so dispensationalists reviving it are like a widow taking her dead husband back.
teachings.text:
Addressing the Jew, brethren after the flesh, those knowing the law, Paul continues his argument that the law is the ministry of death, while the gospel of grace is unto life.

But to buttress the point, Paul uses the law to demonstrate how the law is made null by the death of Christ, just as a marriage is annulled by the death of the husband. The oldness of the letter is done away with for the newness of the Spirit.

Paul is again dismantling the idea of salvation by the law. The same law that Judaizers sought to bring to the new believers of the Gentiles. The same law that dispensationalists claim was the means of salvation for the Jews, and that it will be implemented again. As if a widow should take her dead husband again as a spouse.

 *O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.*

Amen 🙏🏻

teachings.title: The law failed because men failed
teachings.summary: The law failed to produce righteousness because Israel would not execute its judgments, and God's wrath abides on any nation that refuses His statutes.
teachings.text:
We know the law is made to be a schoolmaster to bring Israel to repentance of faith in the Christ to come. That the failing of the law to achieve righteousness wasn't God's fault, but man's.

Because when a man dishonored his father and mother, cursing them, the people didn't put him to death.

Because when a man committed adultery with his neighbor's wife, they weren't put to death.

When a man committed incest, uncovering the nakedness of his own family's women, commiting abominations, the people do not put him to death.

When sodomites were found amongst them, men laying with men, abominations to the Lord, the people suffered them to live rather than stoning them to death, their blood being upon them.

Beastiality, incest, the abomination of sex in the blood of menstruation...all these things that God warns nations about eventually are left unchecked by a wicked and perverse generation. The people didn't follow His statutes.

*Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all my judgments, and do them: that the land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out. And ye shall not walk in the manners of the nation, which I cast out before you: for they committed all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.*

God's wrath abides on a nation that fails to sanctify themselves through his  statutes and judgments. As the nations driven out before the Isralites were condemned. As Israel itself would be. And as nations even to this day find out as the land spews them out for their abominations.

teachings.title: Love thy neighbour came from Leviticus
teachings.summary: The laws against lying, talebearing and partiality flesh out love of neighbour, a commandment from the same God who forbade sexual immorality, not something Jesus invented.
teachings.text:
*Ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another. And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.*

*Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people: neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour; I am the Lord.*

These items flesh out the commandment against bearing false witness, both in rumor and backbiting and in matters before the law. Swearing falsely, profaning the Lord, taking His name in vain. Note it is tied in with stealing, and defrauding people, lying to one another.

Not robbing a man of his wages, but paying what is due as it is due. Not using false weights and measures. Not judging unrighteously, not being a respecter of persons, favoring the rich over the lowly. Not doing favors for a protected class, or for buddies, but dealing squarely.

Cursing the dead (who cannot hear you) or placing a stumbling block before the blind who cannot see, being dishonest in treachery and cruelty.

Do not hate your brother in your heart. This doesn't mean you can't be righteous in anger for a trespass, but it does mean you cannot hold that grudge after reconciliation or redemption is paid. But we are to rebuke our neighbor who is in sin, or who trespasses against us, that they may come to forgivnessand peace with you. Not out of anger or wrath, but love.

Which brings us to the second of the great commandments as Jesus preached; Love thy neighbor as thyself. On this, and on loving God, hangs the whole of the law.

Many modernists believe that Jesus invented this commandment, and that it is in variance with the Old Testament, "more wrathful God." That Jesus "taught love, not division, maaaaan." But they err not knowing scripture.

Those who seek to say that the prohibition against sexual immorality in chapter 18, for example, are done away with by the two great commandments of the NT, ignore that those commandments come from the same exact God in the same exact place in scripture.

teachings.title: The most complete ritual religion ever given
teachings.summary: The priestly ordinances were God giving Israel the most perfect outward ritual religion, holy yet still worldly compared to the spirit of the New Testament, as a schoolmaster.
teachings.text:
Aside from the obvious symbolism of Christ in the blood and burnt offerings, the bread waved before the Lord, the sanctification rituals for Aaron and his sons, the detailed ordinances given to Moses from God is also a perfect example of worldly religion, given as much as a schoolmaster as the rest of the law.

Let me explain my thoughts on this, and by no means is this authoritative but it's how it strikes me at this time, so soon after our study on Hebrews. Like all Biblical teachings, the depth of meaning is great and often multiple meanings can be found in the symbolism that are all correct in their own way. God's word is that deep.

But when we see all these things laid out, a complex series of vestments, offices, specific and detailed sacrifices and the times and days to be honored, we see God giving to the children of Israel the most well thought out and complete ritualistic religion, the outward practices of faith, that the world has ever seen. Natural man may have pantheons and priests, ceremony and holiday and sacrifices, but they seem almost random and simple, obvious traditions of men.

God here provides the ultimate in worship practices along those traditions of men, refined by His mind and reflecting patterns in Heaven, and symbols of the Christ to come. Kept holy by a holy God that there is no sin within it, but still outwardly worldly compared to the spirit of the New Testament.

teachings.title: Not a pattern for chapels and vestments
teachings.summary: The tabernacle priesthood was a schoolmaster showing the failure of earthly rites, not a pattern for grand chapels, robed priests and vestments, since Christ offered one sacrifice for ever.
teachings.text:
And so, God having given Moses perfect law, gives Moses the pattern for the Tabernacle and the priesthood to serve it, taken from Aaron and his sons. This too was a schoolmaster, to show us the failings of the earthly and carnal systems of sacrifices and high offices in the church. Ceremony and rituals that were represented in such perfection and detail, only to fail to deliver righteousness in the end.

*And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: but this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; from henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool*.

Carnal people who practice a false form of the faith, see this and the description given to Solomon for the Temple, and believe that it is instructions for massive chapels and priests in robes and funny hates, and fancy vestments. But the NT shows us that these things were not a pattern for us, but that Christ showed a more perfect way.

The same temples and priests became Pharisees and Sadducees and scribes. The sacrifices made into money changing, and offense to God. It is man who takes God's perfection and makes it into hypocrisy and vanity.

teachings.title: The judgments of God are ever relevant
teachings.summary: Only the ceremonial law was done away in Christ, so Christians should learn the moral judgments of Exodus, which will be enforced in the Millennium where the saints judge.
teachings.text:
Exodus 21 begins the judgments of God that flow from the implications of accepting the covenant with the children of Israel, the 10 Commandments.

*The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple. The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes.*

These statutes given through Moses, the moral law, is part of the covenant of being God's people. The right judgments that make His people holy, even today. None of the moral law was done away with in Christ. Only the ceremonial law, the ordinances and Levitical duties and sacrifices.

**Hebrews 9**
*8 The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:*

*9 Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;*

*10 Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.*

*11 But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;*

*12 Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.*

But His moral law is eternal, and these judgments set as the rules that will be enforced with a rod of iron in the Millennium. We should consider each, and understand the intent behind them all calls back to administration of the 9 commandments that remain following the fulfilment of the Sabbath.

Saved Christians have an obligation to know and understand these judgments and the spirit of their purpose, that we may serve as judges in the Millennial Kingdom.

*But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.*

There's a tendency to gloss over these things as "archaic" or not relevant, but they are ever relevant and key to understanding many of the commands given in the New Testament.

They also are fairly straightforward and need little interpretation. Over the next couple days I will post the chapters pertaining to the law and we can discuss them in chat. There's some misunderstanding and common questions people have, that I can help with, but again it's not very difficult textually.

teachings.title: Ye are they which justify yourselves before men
teachings.summary: The covetous Pharisees derided Jesus because they justified themselves by works before men, missing that the law and prophets were given to bring them to salvation in Christ.
teachings.text:
*And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.*

We see the transition here in chapter 16 of Luke, from Jesus addressing His disciples, to the Pharisees, who hearing His preaching, derided Him. They were covetous, the Bible says.

Covering means to resent those with something we lack coupled with the desire to possess that which isn't ours to have. Covetousness, which is idolatry according to scripture, is a sin because by its very nature shows a lack of gratitude towards God, and makes us bring evil towards our neighbors. Here the Pharisees are hearing Jesus preach on serving God rather than Mammon, not taking care for the things of this world, but rather laying up treasures in Heaven, and Luke, writing in the Spirit points out their covetousness. This preaching offends them. Preaching against sin brings two reactions in those that hear; conviction and repentance towards the truth or despising the messenger and the message, and doubling down in sin.

The Pharisees derided Jesus. Insulted Him. Called Him names and mocked His teachings, that had cut them to the quick.

And Jesus says to them; *Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.*

He says they follow the Law, but since John the Baptist and his preaching of the Kingdom and Christ's coming, the Law is not profitable, salvation is here.

They sought to be made justified by the works they did and the outward appearances they kept up, and by appealing to the justification before men, and when the Gospel of reconciliation is preached to them, where the praise of men matters not, but the humility and faith of a contrite heart towards God saves, they derided Him. They despised the gift.

Like Jesus said to His disciples in the previous verses, the Pharisees couldn't be trusted with the things of this world, they certainly won't be trusted for the things of the world to come.

Jesus says the Law and the prophets were to bring men to salvation when the kingdom of God is preached them. That they be fruit meet for repentance. The Law as a schoolmaster, the prophets giving witness.

Jesus says it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the Law to fail. This has a double meaning, that God's law is perfect and eternal, in its purpose until the kingdom is full and perfect, and the old heavens and earth are passed away. Burnt up.

But more, here, Jesus is saying how hard they cling to the letter of the law, despite their rejection of the kingdom nigh unto them, even as Heaven and earth pass away to make way for the Kingdom. It should have prepared these men to enter into it. Instead it has left them without. They are adulterous to the faith of the prophets. They missed the point of the Law they justified themselves by. They don't see the Christ before them, and missed the point that there are none righteous, no not one. All have come short of the Glory of God.

And so, Jesus tells these covetous and hypocritical "holy men" a parable, the story of Lazarus and the rich man.

We are introduced to a certain rich man. Often in Jesus preaching he uses "a certain man" to indicate someone who is a particular type of person, that we the audience would readily recognize and know. This certain man was rich, dressed in finery, and ate not just well, but sumptuously. We get the picture here, he is very rich. And by implication, someone when covetous Pharisees would see as one justified by the reckoning of man, the way they see themselves. An exaggerated version of their ideal, and in the context of their derision against His preaching on serving Mammon.

And Jesus contrasts this certain rich man with Lazarus, a poor beggar which was laid at the gate of the rich man seeking the crumbs that fell from his plate. Moreover, Lazarus was full of sores, suffering physically, humiliated by the dogs licked his open wounds. Dogs being unclean to the eyes of the Jews. A more pathetic figure couldn't be painted.

teachings.title: The greatest commandment and the scribe near the kingdom
teachings.summary: Jesus summed the law in loving God and neighbour, both quoted from the Old Testament, and the scribe who humbly sought scripture was near the kingdom.
teachings.text:
This scribe is getting it. He knows the scriptures and sees that Jesus has answered all that the Pharisees and Sadducees have come at Him with, as the scribe likely knows the scriptures better than they do, given his station.

And he asks what is a defining question of Christ, to give the greatest commandment of God. And Jesus Christ the Son of God, the word, sums up the whole of the law on two points:
*Love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment. And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.*

Some say here Jesus has invented new doctrine, because they not knowing the scriptures don't know that Jesus has simply quoted the first of the 10 commandments from Exodus and that loving thy neighbor as yourself comes from Leviticus.

On these two points rests the whole of the Law.

(Some like to point at love thy neighbor' as new doctrine, to say Jesus was more liberal and hippy-dippy than the God of the OT, but Leviticus 19:18 where this is found, is located in the same teachings that deal with stoning sodomites and adulterers)

The scribe agrees with Jesus answer, and adds to it from scripture prompting Jesus to say how near the Kingdom he is. Both physically, being in the presence of Christ, and spiritually, being so close to the truth, having faith from the word.

The contrast between this scribe and the Pharisees and Sadducees, is the difference between earnestly seeking the knowledge of God from his word and thinking themselves wise becoming fools.

Many such cases.

People with a predetermined idea of what they want God's word to say cannot be swayed from their belief in themselves. From their own reasoning. But those who earnestly seek wisdom, and humbly allow God's word to reveal it to them gain understanding. It's just how it works.

*For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding. He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous: he is a buckler to them that walk uprightly. He keepeth the paths of judgment, and preserveth the way of his saints*

teachings.title: The law is good if a man use it lawfully
teachings.summary: Paul warns against fables and genealogies but says God's law is good for the lawless and sinners, so it still needs enforcing today against libertarian Christians who take liberty for license.
teachings.text:
So, as we wade into the doctrines laid out here, we see that Timothy is charged with instructing those he finds called to the office of bishop, or pastor as we call it in modern times (terms that come from overseeing a flock of sheep), that they give no heed to fables and genealogies that lead to foolish questions, and don't edify the congregation. This is similarly given to Titus, avoiding Jewish fables and endless genealogies to instruct the future leaders of these churches.

At the time of this writing, many of the apocryphal books had been in circulation, non-inspired and many heretical concepts, being used by Jews and similarly creeping in to the new Christian churches.

The ramifications of rejecting the teachings of the pastoral epistles can still be felt today, with apostate false church of Rome, which uses unqualified men in unbiblical positions and uses the apocrypha, Jewish fables, to create doctrines. Not just the fables of the already existing books during Paul's day, such as using Maccabees to create the lie of purgatory,  but false gospels of Thomas and Andrew, for example, which they've adopted their Mary-worship from.

Of course we have the genealogies attempting to paint "seeds of Abraham" as special, continued in dispensationalist heresy today.

Paul continues to say that, in instruction of these leaders to also stress the importance of *charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.* The gracious love for others that comes from having a good conscience before God, being blameless and regenerate in the faith of Christ. Unfeigned, sincere. While all saved have reconciliation with God regarding their sin, it is a spiritual maturity that brings one to this gracious and merciful charitable love for others.

There are some, Paul informs us, that having neglected this trait, and professing themselves wise, have become fools. Vain jangling. Just pontificating on the matters of the law, and works, and neglecting the faith, and forgiveness and grace. Many such cases, even today.

Paul does caution that the law of God *is good,* in itself, for its purpose, which he lays out here. His admonition is against the legalistic works-based false teachers, not the law itself, which we who are saved have liberty from, but that the law continues to serve as a schoolmaster, and is *for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.* To bring them to the knowledge of the Gospel, or at the very least, to punish wrongdoing on earth and to keep an orderly society, understanding that the majority of people are not saved.

To many people, both believers and naturally, unbelievers, see no benefit or roles in God's law being used today. "That was for those times. Not for today." But, as we see from this list of sins, there is a clear need to maintain God's law regardless of what current year is.

Whoremongers and whores, who defile themselves with mankind, murderers, liars and every other thing that is contrary to good teaching from scripture. It's a broad list, and we understand why there remains a need to enforce these things.

There is an element of libertarian Christian that doesn't just reject the Levitical laws and carnal ordinances, done away with in Christ, but see no need to enforce the laws of God, written in our hearts and proclaimed from Adam on by God. They take their liberty for license to sin, and will not support the role of government and the law to protect people from evil and bring people to the understanding that there is sin and punishment, which is key to coming to repentance and accepting salvation.

teachings.title: The Good Samaritan and the lawyer
teachings.summary: Jesus answered the lawyer that keeping the two great commandments would bring life, then showed through the Good Samaritan that no one actually keeps the law, so none are righteous by works.
teachings.text:
**Luke 10**

*25 And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?*

*26 He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?*

*27 And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.*

*28 And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.*

*29 But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?*

*30 And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.*

*31 And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.*

*32 And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.*

*33 But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him,*

*34 And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.*

*35 And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.*

*36 Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?*

*37 And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.*

This verse is relevant. A lawyer, who in Jesus time was an expert in the OT, the Law of Moses, sought to trick Jesus and asked him in bad faith what must he do to be saved. Jesus turned it around on him and asked what the law says. The lawyer's answer of the 2 great commandments of the Law is *true,* Jesus agrees. That is if one were capable of keeping these two commandments, they would indeed have eternal life. One imagines the lawyer had thought up to this point that he'd make our pretty well under the law, and that he would trip up Jesus. But Jesus answer shook that faith in himself. So seeking to justify himself, to confirm that he was righteous by the law, the lawyer asks Christ to clarify "who is my neighbor?"

The parable Jesus answered with, the Good Samaritan, showed that the enemy of the Jews acted as a loving neighbor where the servants of the spiritual life of Jews failed, revealed the truth of the Law, that none of us hold to it. None of us love our enemies as neighbors. None of us love God with our whole hearts and minds. None of us are righteous by our works.

teachings.title: The letter killeth, but the Spirit giveth life
teachings.summary: The letter of the law condemned us and served as a schoolmaster, while the Spirit gives liberty, and the veil of Moses pictures the veil on Jewish hearts that is taken away when they believe on Christ.
teachings.text:
Paul has begun this letter to Corinth far less hostile than the last. His reproach cooler.

His reframing of the question of letters of commendation to one of the Spirit and the heart of the persons saved by his or those he sent's ministry, that the believers' own salvation and behavior are the real epistles of the authority Paul and the others have is softer, and yet more biting.

He spins from this to the idea of the letters of the law, of the old testament, being what condemned us, knowledge of the law bringing with it sin, which the Bible defines as transgression of the law (**1 John 3:4**), but in the Spirit is Liberty, the eternal life given in the new testament.

This becomes a major theme for Paul in other epistles, the use of the law by God as a schoolmaster, bringing us to sure knowledge of our transgressions and death from sin, and the liberty found in Christ, which is more glorious than even the hand of God engraving stone and giving it to Moses.

The veil Moses wore to protect the Hebrews in the wilderness from the lingering glory of God reflected in his face becomes a metaphor for the veil keeping the glory of God, through Christ, from the hearts of the Jew.

But, with the veil taken away by belief on Christ, we see the glory manifest, and in that image, have it reflect in our own faces, the way it did to Moses, but unhidden and used to show others our faith that they might believe.

teachings.title: The forgiveness of our debt
teachings.summary: The law covenant put Israel in bondage to death, but Christ's blood is a better testament that forgives our debt, the grace God commands us to show others.
teachings.text:
The covenant God made with the Israelites, that by the works of the law they may know Him, and they would be His people , and He would be their God, put the people in bondage. Because by the same law comes the works of death.

For Christ to then set them that believe at liberty, by the grace of the Father to not hold us to that covenant, but by the blood of Christ being a new and better testament, built on better promises, that we have been reconciled despite our sin. Despite our own transgression of the law. That God commendeth His love towards us that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. This is that forgiveness of debt. This is that grace and mercy that He has for us, and commands us to give towards others.

teachings.title: The flaw was with them
teachings.summary: The old covenant ended not because the law was flawed but because the people continued not in it, and a new covenant in Christ replaced it.
teachings.text:
The Lord God of Israel, the Redeemer, our Saviour. His holy Name being witnessed by His people to bring all the nations unto Him for forgiveness, that all may be justified. Held in His hand. Our sins and transgressions remembered no more.

This was the plan for Jacob. This was the plan for His people.

*But thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob; but thou hast been weary of me, O Israel.*

*Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary, and have given Jacob to the curse, and Israel to reproaches.*

This is why their covenant was ended. Not because the law given Moses in the wilderness to deliver unto the people was flawed. But the flaw was in them.

**Hebrews 8:6-9**
*But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

They continued not in His covenant. The flaw was with them.

 *In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.*

The old covenant was ended. A new testament in Christ was established. And every nation carries a righteous remnant of believers. Who are His and of His name. Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: The law was perfect, the fault the people's
teachings.summary: With Joshua as a picture of Christ, he teaches the song of Moses shows the covenant failed because of the people, not the law, which disproves dispensationalism.
teachings.text:
The life of Moses, to whom the law was given, nears its end, and Joshua, a picture of Christ, is given power to lead the children of Israel into the promised land.

Like John, a voice crying out in the wilderness, Moses cleared the way, making the paths straight for the one who would come to bring deliverance.

The book of the law is written, and placed in the Ark that is in the heart of the camp. Done to bear witness of the sins and iniquity of the people. Like the law written in the hearts of man, a conscience, pricked of the Spirit to lay bare our transgressions. To let us know when we have gone astray. As a testimony of the Lord against them who were given the oracles of God. To remind them of their need for His salvation.

An ordinance is given, that in the jubilee year, at the fall feast of Tabernacles, the feast of tents, the people shall gather and hear the reading of the Law. The story of God and His people. His Commandments and His love for them that believe on His name. How he rescued them from bondage and delivered on the promises He made. Every 7 years the people will be reminded. And yet He knows their hearts.

And so the Lord teaches Moses a new song. One to teach the children of Israel that they may know that God knows, they will break the covenant.

This song and its need are all the evidence we need to understand that the fault of the covenant made in the wilderness was always the people. The law itself pure and perfect. The people forsake the God who delivered them, and chase after other gods. God promises to forsake them in turn, for all the evils that they wrought.

Moses, delivering this all to the people before the congregation, reiterates his own knowledge that they will turn aside. That they will utterly corrupt themselves.

Once again, proving dispensationalism to be unbiblical heresy.

teachings.title: Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk
teachings.summary: The command not to seethe a kid in its mother's milk does not ban mixing meat and dairy, and kosher rules are vain traditions while the dietary laws are done away for Christians.
teachings.text:
*Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk.*

What does this mean? Why do Jews forbid the mixing of dairy with meat entirely from this passage?

The act of seething, a form of boiling meat, in this case in milk, was a way of cooking, even basting in butter that which is roasted. It's a wonderful way to enjoy the food that God has blessed us with, but even the idea of using the actual mother's milk to cook her kid seems cruel. But why prohibit it?

The logic of man says that the traditions of the people they were to drive out included this form of cruel sacrifice to their pagan gods. That may be. It could also be symbolism of Christ and a prohibition of the cooking method that they keep it a burnt offering.

But what it does not do is ban dairy with meat generally. The "kosher" practices are just more of the vain traditions of the judaizers. And these dietary laws are done away with for Christians in the New Testament anyway. But it is an interesting verse to chew upon, no pun intended.

teachings.title: The ten commandments covenant ended in Christ
teachings.summary: The Sinai covenant of ten commandments ended in Christ, while its moral content remains in the two great commandments under the better testament.
teachings.text:
And from the mountain God made His covenant with the children of Israel, these 10 commandments. And the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished.

This covenant has ended with Christ. The law of death replaced with the law of liberty.

The moral components remain, covered by the two great commandments reiterated by Jesus in the new testament;

*Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.*

But the promise to Israel that if they kept these 10 commandments they would be God's people, which in their failing to keep was done away with, that a more excellent Testament could take its place, one for all nations given in the Spirit that they may be adopted into the kingdom of God.

teachings.title: New wine in new bottles: a better covenant
teachings.summary: The parables of the new patch and new wine show Jesus was not mending the old covenant but replacing it with a better one, the replacement theology Zionists deny.
teachings.text:
Understanding this, and that the Pharisees had the wrong idea about what fasting's purpose is, and how righteousness is achieved, Jesus replies to their accusation;

*Can ye make the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.*

He says, do you make people who are celebrating to fast? Is that the time or place for it?

Each of us may be called to fast, in our own time and need by the Spirit. But that's not something to judge another by, if your time is now and theirs isn't. You aren't better than they are, or more righteous or spiritual because you've given yourself to fast. And if you're doing it in the correct spirit, you'd know it.

But further, Jesus is saying His time is short. That He will be gone from their presence and they will have time appointed to them for fasting then.

Not content with that upbraiding of these hypocrites, He continues with another parable. Parables are common examples that may be understood on their own, to better illustrate a more difficult concept.

Jesus says, if you have an old garment to mend, you don't sew a new cloth to patch it. Because the new cloth will shrink, it will pull the stitching ripping it worse than it was. That the new isn't in agreement with the old. It doesn't match. It will wear differently.

And in a like manner, newly squeezed juice isn't put into old wine bottles. (Bottles being leather casks, designed to be water-tight to store liquids). Wine in the Bible means all juices, fresh or fermented, and I won't get into that but the drunkards seethe at this when it is pointed out. And new wine, fresh juice, of put into an old, dried out and worn cask, an old bottle, as it begins to ferment will give off gasses, expanding inside the bottle, causing it to be ruined and the wine to spill out. (While they had ways to preserve juice to prevent fermentation into alcohol, for longer term storage, most was pressed and bottled to be consumed before it could naturally occur).

These two examples of things common to that day, before modern mass consumerism gave us plastic bottles and eliminated the need to patch clothing, were things people could understand. And Jesus used it to make a point to the Pharisees who were touting their own righteousness.

They are the torn and ratty clothes. They are the warn and old bottles. What Jesus was bringing was new. A new and better testament. A new and better covenant. He wasn't there to fix the tear they'd made in their disobedience. He was going to replace it.

He wasn't there to refill their old, dried and cracked bottles, but to give new wine in bottles fit to hold it.

He says "*No man also having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better*." He is calling them out and saying why they cannot understand Him or His preaching, or the behavior of those who desired this new thing.

He's saying no wonder you don't get it. They are drunk on old wine. They can't understand the new thing He is replacing the old with.

It is this same point we just studied in **Hebrews 8**;

*But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

 This is the "replacement theology" that Zionists deny.

Jesus is proclaiming **a more excellent ministry,** the mediator of **a better covenant,** which was established upon **better promises.**

It doesn't say *Except for the Jews. Hebrews is literally written to them.

teachings.title: Not Sinai but Mount Sion
teachings.summary: Believers are not under the covenant of Sinai that brought death but come to the heavenly Sion of the new covenant, serving God with reverence.
teachings.text:
Therefore, we are again reminded that we aren't under the covenant of Sinai, but of Zion. We aren't like the Hebrews in the wilderness who, hearing God's voice and His commandments could not endure it and asked that God not speak directly to them any more (as much of fear of His commandments which establish death, as fear of the thunderings of God). We are of the new covenant of a Heavenly Zion, which established life, in the continued presence of the Lord.

*But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect, And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.*

So we shouldn't be as those in the wilderness who turned from the voice of God, but instead glory in it, that He will not only shake the earth but the heavens as well. And so we serve God with grace, and reverence. God-fearing, where our faith brings good report. That we might bear fruit of those led to the straight paths we walk by His light that shines from us.

*Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear:*

*For our God is a consuming fire.*

teachings.title: The Veil Done Away in Christ
teachings.summary: The old covenant had mediators and a veil, but in the new every believer is a priest and temple, so religions restoring priests and sacraments reject the better testament.
teachings.text:
Building on this, and to further cement the understanding that Jews (and all Catholics and Dispensationalist Zionists, many Prots included) are perishing and have not the understanding of scripture.

In the old covenant man was given a process, mediators between them and God. The carnal ordinances and Levitical priesthood, the tabernacle in the wilderness and the temple built by hands, all served as an intermediary between God and His people. The reading of the law given in synagogues. The sin offering and free will offering and every sacrifice, the religious ordinances, feast and days, all a picture towards Christ to come, and administered by the Mosaic system given in the Old Covenant. The veil between Moses and the people. The veil between the Holy of Holies and the people.

But the people were blinded and *unto this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament.*

This veil is only done away with in  Christ.

And the law which condemned, that glorious, perfect law of God, which served as a schoolmaster to bring to the people the knowledge of sin and their need for salvation. The law which as we saw in Hebrews 8 was perfect, but the people failed. And so a better testament is given us.

*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.
