For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:*

And so there is no longer a priesthood, we are all preists.
No longer a temple, we are all each of us a temple.
No longer a human mediator, Jesus is our High Priest.
No longer a nation of the flesh, but a spiritual nation of believers looking forward to that better country.
No longer a vail between God and man, Jesus tore it forever.

And so the false religions that deny this better Testament and deny the truth of the new covenant, and who place temples and preists and sacraments and ceremony between man and God, and the burden of the law upon man's shoulders, all stems from the fact that the Gospel is foolishness to them that remain perishing. That the natural man receiveth not the things of God.

teachings.title: The Tabernacle and the Better Covenant
teachings.summary: Under the new covenant God's Spirit and law dwell in believers, making each a temple and priest with direct access through Christ.
teachings.text:
And so, in the Old Testament we have the tabernacle, where the Spirit of God resided, the law (ark of the covenant) was present, the shadows of things to come, prophesying Christ were contained and which was where the sacrifices that pointed towards Jesus took place.

But the new, the better covenant, the Spirit of God resides in us, the law upon our hearts, the shadows of things fufifiled, Jesus as the only and final sacrifice for sin.

It isn't the nature of the promise, nor is it God's mercy and grace that changed. It wasn't the faith in Christ which was always the means of salvation that vanished away. Or waxed old to be burned.

What changed was the way in which God's Spirit and law presented itself. And the means by which we interacted with Him, for the preists served as a functionary to the assembly, but now, in Christ who is our High Priest after the order of Melchisedek, we obtain a direct relationship with God. We become a holy priesthood. We become a separate nation. Each a temple of God.

teachings.title: Sarah's life an allegory of believing Israel
teachings.summary: Sarah's life pictures faithful Old Testament Israel saved by faith in the promise, while Hagar and Ishmael picture Israel after the flesh, cast out.
teachings.text:
Now, as the Bible in **Galatians 4** says, regarding the story of Sarah and Isaac, that these things be an allegory, the children of the promise in Sarah, the children after the bondage of the law, in Hagar. That the true seed of Abraham isn't after the flesh, as Ishmael was by the bondwoman Hagar, but by the miracle of God, Issac, conceived in faith through Sarah.

The life story of Sarah represents Old Testament Israel, faithful believing Israel, who were saved through faith in the promise made to Abraham. An allegory, as the Bible says.

When we first meet Sarah, as a young wife to Abraham, we are told she was barren. Without hope of conception. She journeys to Canaan, the promised land.

Later, due to famine, she sojourns into Egypt, is captured by Pharaoh, and God for Sarah's sake visits plagues upon the Pharoah's house until he relents and sends Sarah, Abraham, Lot and their cattle and belongings out from Egypt. Just as the Israelites spoiled Egypt, and went out with them, a mixed multitude.

Sarah, despite her faith and love of God lapses in faith, and brings adultery to the bed of Abraham, with Hagar. Sarah's impatience with God's promise has her seek to find an heir after the flesh. Just as the Israelites lapsed in faith and brought the adultery of strange gods at times, and eventually sought an earthly king to rule them, frustrated at the timing of God.

And like Israel, which would at times repent and turn back to God, admitting their error, Sarah says to Abraham; *My wrong be upon thee: I have given my maid into thy bosom; and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes: the Lord judge between me and thee.*

And Hagar, having fled from Sarah with Ishmael the heir after the law, representing Israel after the flesh, not of faith, was given another chance by God, so too were the Jews of Jesus earthly ministry, to receive the adoption by faith that they though was theirs by law. And Sarah, believing Israel, gave them a home until the coming of Isaac.

We are told of another captivity, Sarah taken by a king, and freed not by plagues but by the fear of the Lord upon Abimelech, convicted of his error, just as Babylonian captivity was.

And when Isaac was born, Ishmael mocked the heir of the promise, and Sarah cast out the bondwoman and her son, though it grieved Abraham, the father. But God agrees with Sarah that son after the flesh, the heir according to the law be cast out, so that the son of faith may come in to his inheritance in full. Just as the non-believing Jews were cut off.

(God, in His mercy offers salvation to Hagar if she just believe. And a well of water giving her salvation, just as any seed of Abraham after the flesh can still repent towards Christ today)

Finally, Sarah having seen her son born of a miracle and come to be offered as a sacrifice, (I believe at 33 upon a hill in Jerusalem, spared by God, a picture of Jesus) she passes away a year later, at 127 years old and is honored, being given a place with the patriarchs, our being told of her end, chronicled by scripture. And in her faith, she was saved, and through her, all nations and kindreds were blessed.

teachings.title: Do ye not hear the law? The bondwoman and the free
teachings.summary: Paul's Hagar-Sarah allegory warns that adding works of the law to faith puts men under bondage, while salvation is God's free gift that cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
And so with this better understanding of the allegory, of recognizing that the entire Old Testament is about Christ Jesus and salvation by faith alone in him, to redeem us, offered by God the father in love and grace, we can understand the righteous anger of Paul writing unto the Galatians.

The Church of the Galatians being swayed by judaizers into accepting another gospel, one of bondage to the law. Whereby they were being told that they must circumcise, keep the days and the months and the dietary laws in the carnal ordinances to be saved. Being dragged back to Hagar, the Bond woman and rejecting Sarah and the son of the promise. Of faith.

And Paul writes, "*O foolish Galatians! who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?"* The Apostle is angry, he says he fears them. He says that he doubts their salvation, which he had labored with them and questions if it was in vain. Paul saying that only an unsaved person who didn't believe the gospel of Faith he presented them would be susceptible to the judaizers dragging them back under the law and away from the liberty of Christ.

*My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you,I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.*

 *Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?*

*For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.*

*But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise.*
*Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants.*

He says that he's willing to go through this again with them that they may come to Jesus. That they seeking to be brought back under the law, he says don't you even hear the law? And this is what prompts his use of Sarah and Hagar as an allegory. As a teaching moment taken from scripture that they may understand the difference between salvation by faith alone and the bondage of the law.

This is the same message we can give to those claiming Christ who have added works of the law to the salvation given in the simple Gospel of reconciliation and faith.

These judaizers and those bewitched by them will claim that, "Yes it's by faith alone but you have to do the works of the law to be saved. You have to adhere to our vain traditions. To our carnal ordinances. To our dietary restrictions. You don't expect to just be handed salvation? Do you?"

And so they bring people to be the seed after Hagar, not Sarah. And like Ishmael, they do not receive the inheritance which is given by faith in God's promise, not by heirs according to the law.

Just as Sarah was barren from birth, and brought to old age, it took a miracle of God, visited upon her, to bring her the promise. Not by anything she did, for she was not capable, but in God all things are possible.

This is the lesson. *Do you not hear the law?*

If you're trusting in your own works, if you're sewing your own fig leaves, if you're offering the fruit of your garden, instead of the firstling of the flock, if you're committing adultery with Hagar to produce your salvation, repent. Hear the law.

Salvation is given us by God, in His grace, through His Son, Jesus Christ, killed for our sins, a burnt offering, raised from the dead, that we may be redeemed in faith and sealed by the Holy Spirit unto the day of redemption. A free gift that once accepted cannot be lost. Eternal life. Heir to the Kingdom. Sons of God.

teachings.title: Cast out the bondwoman and her son
teachings.summary: Ishmael cast out pictures those who seek justification by works of the law, including Talmudic Jews and all works religions, while the children of faith inherit.
teachings.text:
This theme, of the elder of the flesh being rejected for the son of the spirit, of the promise, exists to teach us the way in which we who are sons of God in faith are the true heirs after Abraham, and those of the flesh who rejected Christ, are like Ishmael. Cast out.

In Genesis 21, in accordance with Sarah's wishes and the Lord's command, Abraham reluctantly banishes his firstborn, Ishmael, and the boy's mother, the slave Hagar.

Just as those under the law, using their own works to justify themselves before God, are cast out. Children of the bondwoman. But those who were conceived by faith, like Issac was, the saved believers justified in Christ, receive the inheritance.

And this extends not only to those Jews who developed the Talmudic Judasism that spun out of the Phariseitical line following the death and resurrection of Jesus, but to all works-based false religion.

In Galatians, Paul writes warning against those Judaizers who seek to put the foolish Galatians back under bondage. They've always been those seeking to undermine the faith that calls upon the name of the Lord for salvation. From the fig leaves in the garden to Cain bringing his vegetables and fruit that he labored to grow. Right unto today with Catholic sacrament and works, Buddhist and Hindu and Muslims. And of course Jews of every stripe.

Now Ismael is said to be the father of what would be Islam, that the son of the bondwoman's promised seed were of the Arabs and Mohamed. And their acceptance of Jesus as a prophet, but denying His sacrifice to instead trust in their own works, a reflection of the sin of Sarah and Abraham with Hagar. It's an interesting correlation, given us by revelation in God's word.

teachings.title: God's covenant with Noah
teachings.summary: After the flood God allowed all meat but blood, instituted capital punishment for murder because man is in God's image, and gave the rainbow covenant.
teachings.text:
God blesses Noah and his sons, gives commandments and a covenant with all living things in the earth.

Blessings, commandments and promises. This is the pattern of things with God when those who are faithful and saved by His grace walk with God.

God here tells Noah and his sons to be fruitful and multiply, birthing all nations of man. To that end, he reminds them that all animals are meat to eat, with no restrictions.

Of the clean and unclean animals they may eat, but only the clean for sacrifice to God, being they represent Christ Jesus. As we saw in Chapter 7, Noah had seven pair, male and female of every clean beast, that he could give sacrifice in thanksgiving to God for saving his family in chapter 8.

But there is no restriction on what they can eat, provided they drain the blood, the life thereof. Of that they should not eat. This was replaced for a time for Israel with strict dietary laws against eating unclean beasts under Mosaic law, which along with the priestly and carnal ordinances were done away with in Christ.

God institutes the death penalty and capital punishment for the shedding of blood. Before the flood, from Cain on, the requirement for blood didn't exist, and evil propagated. Here, God established a new understanding for man; that we were to enforce His law, blood for blood *for in the image of God made he man*.

God commands again that man be fruitful and multiply. Replenish the earth, bringing forth life abundantly.

God promises all life that He would never destroy the earth and all living things again by flood. He gives the rainbow as His reminder, a token of the covenant between Him and the earth.

*And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.*

teachings.title: The blood of the covenant and thanksgiving
teachings.summary: The Old Covenant sacrifices sealed in blood pictured Christ's once-for-all sacrifice, and God never needed them but desires thanksgiving, mercy and right judgment.
teachings.text:
The covenant was made by sacrifice; the blood of the covenant made by Moses and the people with God was sealed with blood that represented the blood of Christ, and the promise of a better covenant with God by sacrifice, the sacrifice of the Son.

**Hebrews 9:19–23**
*For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.*

The heavens declare the righteousness of Christ Jesus, and His righteousness is upon all His people. God is the judge Himself. The Atonement, Himself. The mediator, Himself.

The saints are secure in His righteousness. But God speaks to Israel in judgment. Beginning with His people.

*Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee: I am God, even thy God.*

The future prophecy versus the current call.

The continuous sacrifices made before God to give the physical nation of Israel the honor of being His people, keep His hand from reproving them harshly. They maintained the Levitical ordinances which He based promises on. The sacrifices that needed to be done constantly to maintain ritual cleanliness and keep His presence among them had been done. He isn't asking for more sacrifice. No additional bulls or goats to shed their blood.

Again, we have a better sacrifice, once and for all, a covenant made by the blood of Jesus, the burnt offering for our sin.

**Hebrews 9:11–14**
*But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?*

But, in the old covenant, the blood of bulls and goats were used, continually, signifying the Sacrifice to come, and this the Levites did.

God is telling His people at this time He isn't asking for more, and in fact it is not the blood of bulls and goats, and their burnt offering that He seeks.

Every beast is His. The cattle upon a thousand hills. If He were hungry, and in need of the savour of the fat and the sustenance of meats, He has His pick and fill. He doesn't need them. Their sacrifices are a picture and a necessity for the covenant, but they do not please Him in and of themselves.

**Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

Sentiment repeated by Christ;

**Matthew 12:7**
*But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.*

Here, in **Psalm 50**, God makes it clear that the offering is thanksgiving. They are vows to be paid to maintain their part in the covenant as His nation. Tithes and first fruits as acts of faith.

It is not, as other gods, a meal for Him to consume, but a thanksgiving offered to show gratitude for all that He has supplied them, and to keep themselves unspotted, and be His people.

God desires mercy towards others. Right judgment, defending the weak and hating the workers of iniquity.

teachings.title: Did ye at all fast unto me?
teachings.summary: God rejected the exiles' self-made fasts because what pleases Him is true judgment, mercy and care for widows and the fatherless, not religious ritual.
teachings.text:
Here, in the return from the exile in Babylon, the people send men to Jerusalem to inquire about the fasting the Jews had begun while in captivity. They would "weep" during the 5th month, Av, commemorating the time of the desolation of Jerusalem and destruction of the temple. Fasting over their loss.

**2 Kings 25:8-9**
*And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, unto Jerusalem: And he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man's house burnt he with fire.*

And the Lord mentions the similar fast in the 7th month, commemorating the slaying of the Jewish governor Babylon had set over the people;

*And as for the people that remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler....But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah.*

But the word of the Lord comes to the prophet, asking *When ye fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh month, even those seventy years, did ye at all fast unto me, even to me?*

Their fasts were self-centered, remembering their own woes, not to God to bring them out of the situation. Neither were their feasts, when they ate and drank, it was for themselves, not to honor Him.

He references the prophets that came before the captivity, Isaiah and Jeremiah and others, who told them what to do to get right and avoid the destruction that came. To show judgment and mercy. Not grand acts of fasting and weeping.

When things were good, they ignored the prophets. As things improved with the end of captivity, they still hadn't learned the lesson in many ways.

*Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, Execute true judgment, and shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother: And oppress not the widow, nor the fatherless, the stranger, nor the poor; and let none of you imagine evil against his brother in your heart.*

This is what is pleasing to God, not the blood of bulls and goats. Not the religious acts of piety. Not fasts and rituals. To do unto others. To love thy neighbor. To care for the fatherless and widows.

**James 1:27**
*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

This is what God expects of His people. But they had hardened their hearts. And so God says when He cried to them, they wouldn't hear, and so when they would weep for Jerusalem and the Temple, ultimately for themselves, He would not hear them. That He made Jerusalem desolate for their failure to hear. They should be more worried about that judgment than if they should continue in fasts they invented to console themselves.

teachings.title: Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord
teachings.summary: Performative worship and sacrifices without faith and mercy do not please God, as with Catholic and Zionist religion today, and such will face His wrath.
teachings.text:
*Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.*

Those unsaved masses calling for the day of the Lord to escape the judgment against them for their wickedness, God compares to a man fleeing a lion and meeting a bear, or seeking shelter in a house, only to be bitten by a snake.

So too, the fake believers in their solemn assemblies, offering sacrifices as if that's what justifies them before God, and calling upon Him to come quickly...they are the very reason God's wrath is upon them.

**Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

Performative acts of worship, in Ephraim, to a golden calf worshipped in His name, do not please God. The blood of bulls and goats never washed away their sin. He took no pleasure in their songs and burnt offerings while they lived without faith, mercy and right judgement. Disobedient to the commandments that God gave them that it be well with them, and they should live long in the land.

God reminds us that the children of Israel in the wilderness offered sacrifices at the Tabernacle for 40 years, and yet they did not enter the promised land.

How much worse these who have borne the tabernacle of Moloch and Chiun, false and foreign gods, and the images thereof, including the star of their false God, which they invented themselves. Today they call it the star of David.

This message is obviously very relevant. Today we have Catholic-made churches claiming to worship the true Lord, with idols and sacrifices of bread and wine made to them. We have evangelicals yoked to unbelieving Jews, trying to hasten the day of the Lord, and carrying the star of their god.

And God of hosts, the Lord, Christ Jesus, will destroy them and carry them into captivity when that great and wonderful day comes. And there will be darkness and lamentation, wailing and gnashing of teeth.

teachings.title: Do justly and walk humbly with thy God
teachings.summary: God is pleased not by blood offerings, which only pictured Christ, but by faith, mercy and judgment, and religious trappings without faith are dead works.
teachings.text:
**Micah 6** sees the prophet giving to the people of Israel the testimony of the Lord, Who is making His case to the world against those who had been His people.

And even as Balaam could not but speak the words God gave him to speak, the prophet Micah rings out the charges against his countrymen.

The Lord reminds them of His grace towards them, leading them out of Egypt, delivering them through the wilderness into the land they now possess (though not for long).

He reminds them of Balaam being unable to curse them, at Balak the Moabite's hire. The righteousness of God is evident in the righteousness of the people. *How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? or how shall I defy, whom the Lord hath not defied?*

But even so, the council of Balaam was that if you wanted to curse the children of Israel, Balak had to make them sin against the Lord. And so Moab sent her daughters to commit whoredoms with fornication and bringing idols and false gods among them, until God sent a plague to smites His people, they had brought a curse on themselves.

The Lord reiterates His often stated position that it isn't the blood of rams and goats that pleases Him, but faith and mercy and judgement. To do justly and walk humbly with God.

The blood offerings were a picture of Christ. Not the means of salvation themselves. What good are dead works if they aren't given in faith? Trappings of religion rather than pure religion, undefiled;

**James 1:27**
*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

As Jesus rebuked the Pharisees;

**Matthew 23:23**
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.*

In His displeasure, God tells them that His longsuffering mercy is over. That those who deal violently, dishonestly and with lies are now going to be punished by His wrath, and none shall stand.

*Therefore also will I make thee sick in smiting thee, in making thee desolate because of thy sins. Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy casting down shall be in the midst of thee; and thou shalt take hold, but shalt not deliver; and that which thou deliverest will I give up to the sword. Thou shalt sow, but thou shalt not reap; thou shalt tread the olives, but thou shalt not anoint thee with oil; and sweet wine, but shalt not drink wine.*

They walk in the statutes of Ahab and his wicked father, Omri. Worshiping false gods while doing wickedly. And now they will be made a desolation. A reproach. A hissing. A warning and parable among the nations. God revealed by His wrath upon those who were His people, and who chose to go the way of Balaam instead.

teachings.title: God desires mercy, not sacrifice
teachings.summary: Sacrifices were always for man's benefit, pointing to Christ's once-for-all offering, and God desires obedience, confession and mercy toward others.
teachings.text:
God delighting in mercy and right judgement over sacrifices is a theme of scripture.

**Psalm 51:16-17**
*For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.*

**Psalm 40:6-8**
*Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.*

**Isaiah 1:11**
*To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the Lord: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.*

**Jeremiah 7:21-23**
*Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.*

**Hebrews 10:4-10**
*For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure. Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God. Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law. Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.*

The sacrifices were always for man, not God. Even the greatest and only true sacrifice for sin, the blood of Christ Jesus, is for our benefit, not God's.

He wishes us to seek Him. To obey, and to confess to Him when we fall short. To turn to Him continually. And to show mercy and judgement and love, one to another. Forgiving and being forgiven. Being sown in righteousness by faith, and reaping the fruit, bringing in the sheaves. Others brought to the truth, calling upon the name of the Lord. Taking care of the widow. Judging the fatherless. Esteeming the profit of others more than ourselves.

The sacrifices were to show the Israelites of Christ to come, and satisfy that itch in us that there must be blood to pay for our inequities.

Upon the unrighteous, blood is required of blood. But the purpose of Jesus' sacrifice is that we have settled that debt of sin forever, washed clean in His blood, that we may go forth in mercy and His light so shine from us.

teachings.title: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice
teachings.summary: The sacrifices only pictured Christ, the one true offering, and God's will is that we know Him and show others the mercy He showed us, unlike goodness that fades like the morning dew.
teachings.text:
Hosea continues prophesying against Israel, primarily Ephraim and here, Gilead which is a territory of Manasseh, East of the Jordan, but also the Southern Kingdom of Judah. There are false gods, idols, and worse, violence and murder among them.

The prophet begins with an appeal to repentance, turning towards the Lord to heal that which He has smitten them with in His righteous wrath. He says if they do, on the 3rd day they would be risen up, a prophetic reference to the resurrection of Christ.

He says, *Then shall we know, if we follow in to know the Lord: his going forth is prepared as the morning*; Christ's coming was preordained and as inevitable as the sunrise, the morning star. His coming as the rain, the former rains of the spring, the later rains of fall and the harvest. I believe that is prophetic of the two comings of Jesus. Just as the Spring and Fall feasts point to His first and second coming. These rains bringing life in abundance.

He follows this comparison of Jesus to the seasonal rains with a lament if the goodness of Israel, which Hosea compares to the fleeting morning cloud, or the quick to evaporate dew upon the grass.

In relation to the Christian life, I have experienced this of myself. The intents of the morning to pick up that cross, beginning the day with prayer and scripture, only to see the goodness fade with the day like the dew. Drawing the stray moisture from the air around us, rather than being soaked in the rains, and so losing steam throughout the day.

The Lord has slain them with His word, reproved by the prophets speaking in the Spirit, the law convicting them for their deeds. His judgments as a light, piercing the darkness of their sin.

*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

**Psalm 40:6-8**
*Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart*.

**Hebrews 10:7-10**
*Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God. Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all*.

God's will for us is that we show the same mercy towards others He extended to us. The sacrifices and ordinances of the OT were for their understanding, that the children of God had a means of picturing the sacrifice of Christ to come, Jesus being the only true sacrifice for sin. But the blood of the testament with God for forgiveness and eternal life exists as a gift for our benefit, that we may know we have that relationship. That we become sons of God, so that we may know love. Mercy. Charity. His will for our lives and our obedience, that it be well with us. Jesus is the door. But there is a pasture He leads us to, in rest that we can magnify His light to guide others from the darkness.

teachings.title: Eye for eye is God's law, not Hammurabi's
teachings.summary: Eye for eye is God's just law for magistrates, while Jesus calls believers personally to mercy, and the two are complementary rather than contradictory.
teachings.text:
The second half of the chapter begins with a narrative of a child of Egyptian heritage born into the Tribe of Dan, blaspheming God, and God's instructions to take him without the camp and those who heard the blasphemy to stone him to death.

God reiterates that even strangers among them are under His law, both to their good, and to their punishment for violating it.

He says His law is justice, that a murderer be put to death. That blemish, or physical harm, be answered in a like manner; breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth.

This concept of God's law has been understood for millennia, preserved for all time, but in 1901 a Babylonian relic was found that contained what is called Hammurabi's Code, a list of laws credited to the ancient king by archeologists, which included the eye for an eye form of justice.

During the 20th century, what was part of God's perfect law (repeated from **Exodus 21:24-25**
*Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot*, *Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe*) began to be credited to a man, and after it had permeated culture that the concept of an eye for an eye actually originated from Hammurabi's Code, people began to mistakenly think it wasn't God's perfect law. And once they'd managed to mislead people with that, they then began to discredit the concept as barbaric, a remnant of ancient Babylon and not the commandments of God.

And so by the close of the 20th Century, most people had no idea that this was found in scripture, and were taught to think of it as a savage injustice.

If the concept was raised by Christians at all, it was in the context of **Matthew 5:38-39**; *Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.* And this was taught as somehow Jesus contradicting the concept, as if He wasn't the author of it. When Jesus says love thy neighbor, The same people pretend it was a new commandment when it comes from Leviticus as well.

But Jesus calling those who are saved by faith in Him to love even our enemies, to pray for them, to not answer violence with violence, but to show mercy and love to them, isn't saying that the law itself is unjust, for it will be the law in the Millennial Kingdom. He's talking about our hearts storing up wrath, vengeance, and hatred.

Before a magistrate, the eye taken for an eye would still be justice.

**1 Timothy 1:9-11**
*Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

But we who are righteous should forgive those who wronged us and show mercy to those in need. These two concepts aren't contradictory but complimentary.

Our mercy doesn't upend the law. Our being at liberty from the law spiritually means we should be more circumspect in how we view our enemies. Our trust in God for vengeance taking priority over our executing our own wrath.

But if the law demands restitution, so be it. The sword is not wielded in vain.

What those who seek to undermine confidence in scripture do is trust that Christians won't be able to rightly divide the word of God, and this higher level concept would escape us, and lead us to showing perverse judgment.

If you notice, by abandoning the law for the unrighteous, instead of mercy and love and limited restitution to a like-for-like code, we have a "justice system" that either punishes the wrong doer far exceeding what is right in the eyes of God, or not doing anything to rightly punish the wicked and protect the innocent. Those that deserve death still live, often freed to offend again.

teachings.title: Justice in the world, meekness in the believer
teachings.summary: Believers must be meek peacemakers personally while God's law should still be upheld by the state, and ignoring this has left society with neither justice nor mercy.
teachings.text:
The nuance required to understand these differences, The worldly application of biblical principles with people who aren't believers versus how believers should respond personally. This causes confusion for many in other applications such as application of Romans 13 and 14.

Christians are called to be meek, to be peacemakers, to be humble in realizing that our condition is by the grace of God and not of ourselves. To be understanding of our enemies that by love, we may overcome it and bring them to the same peace that we have found in the grace of God.

But that doesn't mean that in this world, God's law shouldn't be upheld. And if we were to stone to death, someone for a capital violation, We should not do so gleefully and with vengeance but with understanding. And after applying just mercy.

By not walking this line, we have a society wherein there is no justice and there is no mercy.

We have courts that are grossly unfair. We have a criminal justice system that can't decide between rehabilitation and punishment and so attains neither.

We don't put to death those who have their own blood upon them. And we lock up people who could have simply worked off the harm they caused. The application of the law becomes arbitrary and capricious rather than circumspect and done with discernment.

teachings.title: God's law is perfect, we are not
teachings.summary: The tension between justice and mercy lies in us, since we want vengeance where God wants justice, and staying in the word makes His judgment clearer.
teachings.text:
I don't know if I'm explaining this concept well, and I myself struggle with the seeming dichotomy. But we have to understand that it isn't God's law that is imperfect, it is us.

We want vengeance and God wants justice. We want mercy when it applies to us but deny it to others, Just as God's mercy is extended to us by His grace, but the wages of sin is a debt we all owe. And a person's blood is upon themselves when they violate God's law.

This I think is why it's so important to stay in God's word, to feed the new man. These concepts become clearer and we begin to see the nuances and glory in how perfect God's judgment is.

teachings.title: God desired not sacrifice
teachings.summary: The carnal ordinances show the futility of trusting priests and sacraments, since God desires mercy and a contrite heart and only faith in Christ's blood remits sin.
teachings.text:
If by the law we learn that all have fallen short and are in need of salvation, then by the carnal ordinances of the law we see the futility and eventual corruption of a priestly class administering materialist rites and sacraments.

In other words, this was all given that both the faithful of the Old Testament had symbols of Christ that they may understand the hearing of the word and by it have faith, over centuries and generations, but also to serve to us that come to faith after Christ the vanity of trusting in such things. That even with the perfect expression of faith in the offerings for sin and the rest, it doesn't work. Only faith and the grace of God through the blood of Jesus can give remission of sin.

*Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law.*

**Psalm 51**
*For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.*

**Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

These things were put in place by God not because He desired them, but because man does. Man needs to see it. To touch it, smell it, experience it in the flesh. They had not the indwelling of the Holy Spirit as we do in the New Testament. So it served a like purpose, and it appeals to natural men and even some overly sensual believers to this day.

teachings.title: Call the sabbath a delight
teachings.summary: The Sabbath in Isaiah 58 is spoken of as Him, Christ, and keeping it means resting in Jesus and lifting the burdens of others.
teachings.text:
*Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity*.

The Lord promises us redemption, restoration. The reestablishment of our nation. Blessings and hope for many generations after us. He seeks mercy and righteous judgment, not the blood of bulls and goats. Not fastings and vain words.

*If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words:*

Notice something here, that the word says the Sabbath is a "Him." The delight of the Holy One. Christ Jesus. Doing that which He did. Healing the sick. Tending to the broken hearted. The Lord of the Sabbath calling us to take the time, ceasing from our labors to help others. Not to be a burden, but to lift others from theirs. To rest in Jesus.

And delight ourselves in the Lord. Amen

teachings.title: Clean and unclean meats done away in Christ
teachings.summary: He teaches the dietary laws were carnal ordinances picturing separation from the Gentiles until the reformation in Christ, and the peculiar people now are those cleansed by His blood.
teachings.text:
*These are the statutes and judgments, which ye shall observe to do in the land, which the Lord God of thy fathers giveth thee to possess it, all the days that ye live upon the earth.*

**Deuteronomy 14** continues the retelling of the law, originally given in the wilderness but now updated slightly for the settling of the promised land.

Here in chapter 14, following a warning against participating in scaring and ritual shavings that the heathens practiced in Canaan before them, mourning rituals that saw them shave their heads in unsightly ways, the Lord gives dietary laws against eating "unclean" beasts. Ordinances that had applied only to the Levites in the desert, but now apply to the Hebrew people as a whole.

*For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.*

Carnal ordinances given as a picture of the time to come, the reformation in Christ;

**Hebrews 9:9-10**
*Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;*
*Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.*

Dietary laws regarding clean and unclean were a sign given to show the separation from the Gentiles, a difference done away with in the New Testament. As the Lord showed Peter in **Acts 10:13-15**;

*And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat. But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean. And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.*

Here, not only lifting the ordinances but encouraging Peter and the other Apostles to give the gospel to the Gentiles. That the holy people were of the Spirit of faith. The peculiar people who God cleansed with the blood of the lamb, echoing Deuteronomy here in this epistle;

**1 Peter 2:9**
*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light*

teachings.title: The dietary laws a living parable of holiness
teachings.summary: The clean and unclean food laws were a schoolmaster teaching holiness, done away in Christ, so we are holy by the heart and not by what we eat.
teachings.text:
The dietary laws of the Levitical priesthood were part of a series of ordinances and rites of cleanliness that served as a way *to make a difference between the unclean and the clean.* To provide this distinction as a lesson to the people, the law being a schoolmaster, that they may better understand the holiness of God.

*Ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.*

As Peter writes in his first epistle, declaring the priesthood of the believer, *Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy.*

It is an example. A means of separation that the Lord instituted with Moses and Aaron to demonstrate this concept. A living parable.

But as Christ Jesus says, it's not what goes into our mouth that is unclean, but the spirit by which it is received, and what proceeds out of our own mouth. And we know that out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

The Isralites were given a chance to commune in assembly with God. To see their faith in His salvation be practiced before them with the ceremonial washings and sacrifices. To witness the spiritual through the physical, that they may come to understand God, and in it, Christ.

Now the time of reformation had come, the death and resurrection of Christ, and these carnal ordinances and diverse washings and sacrifices and oblations were done away with.

**Hebrews 7:11-12**
*If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron? For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.*

And as Peter has revealed to him by God, that the "unclean," the people who were not a people, the Gentiles, were now to be folded into the promise of the kingdom, of the "clean."

*What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.*

And so now, graft in, we are called to be holy for He is holy. Not by the food we eat. Not by the things that enter into the mouth, by what's in our hearts and what we profess.

teachings.title: Ordinances were pictures, not idols
teachings.summary: The Old Testament ordinances like the sabbath were shadows of Christ ended at the cross, but the Pharisees, like Israel with the brazen serpent, made the picture an idol and a work of self-righteousness.
teachings.text:
In chapter 5, and now again in Luke chapter 6, we see the Pharisees seeking to accuse Jesus, that they may discredit Him and His growing ministry. Particularly, they are seeking to shame Him and His disciples for their failure to keep certain ordinances, carnal ceremony, given both by tradition and under the law of Moses, among these ordinances are things like the fasting of meats(food), ceremonial washings(**Matthew 15:12**) and the keeping of the sabbath, the day of rest, as we see here.

The Bible says these ordinances were given in the OT as a picture, a shadow, to remind the people of the promise of the coming Christ, that they not forget and hold fast to the faith preached unto them, until the *day of reformation*. That is, until the things they are foreshadowing come true. Until Christ comes. At that time Jesus figuratively nails them to the cross with Himself. They are over and done, having served their purpose.

And, with the ordinances ended, the Bible says, so too was the regard God had for the nation of Israel. They were to either believe or perish, the same as the Gentiles. Thus the destruction of the Temple in 70AD, least any confusion remain.

And of these ordinances, the keeping of the sabbath was probably the most important, that the people would enter into God's rest, understanding that His work was finished at the time of creation. A picture man could understand, working 6 days and resting the 7th as God did. Forbidden work, because God did it all in regards to salvation. It is a picture of salvation by faith alone in His perfect, meaning complete, works, finished by the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

But man is simple, and foolish and superstitious. The things of God that are a physical picture of the spiritual application He seeks to teach us, becomes an end unto itself in vain tradition. Many, with an autistically literal approach, put the power in the picture, not the things that are being pictured.

And example is given in the OT, in **Numbers 21** where by unbelief the Hebrews in the desert were beset by poisonous snakes, fiery serpents. Many were bit and were dying in agony. God, as an object lesson in the Christ to come, had Moses lift up a brazen snake, made of molten brass and formed, upon a tall wooden pole. This represented Christ and the crucifixion, where Jesus became all sin for us. He said to the people if you look up on this picture of salvation you'll be healed. Lesson learned.

We know this was a picture of Jesus, because it was explained in **John 3**:

*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.*

But we are told that hundreds of years later, the Israelites had lost the purpose and understanding that this picture served. In **2 Kings 4** Hezekiah became king and had to right many of the wrongs in the land;

*He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.*

The picture of the spiritual became a physical idol. The Heavenly lesson became bonds of the carnal.

This is where the Pharisees, Sadducees and scribes are at in the time of Christ. They have lost sight of the spiritual application for these things, and worship the symbol instead.

And so the carnal ordinances were to them an idol. And the work of their flesh in keeping these things replaced their faith in the Lord. They became self-righteous. They used the keeping of these ordinances as how one becomes righteous, rather than faith in what it represents, the Christ to come. And so, they become holier than thou  hypocrites. And later, Judaizers seeking to impose their vain traditions on the newly born again Gentiles. Circumcision, sacrifices, and the keeping of holy days such as the sabbath.

teachings.title: The sabbath fulfilled in Christ
teachings.summary: The sabbath pictured our rest in Christ without works, so no day is esteemed above another and our works now serve to seek the lost.
teachings.text:
There are quite a few things going on in this chapter, lots of doctrine and preaching by Christ, mostly against the holy men of Judah, the scribes and Pharisees. Those who had been entrusted with teaching and keeping God's will, and who had perverted it to be hypocritical vipers.

They reproach Jesus and His disciples for gleaning and eating corn on a sabbath, Jesus reminds them of scripture, that the man of God and those with them may profane the day if doing God's will.

Soon, the sabbath would be done away with in Christ, where no day would be esteemed above another. Our rest in Him. A picture of not working on the day of rest, we are entered into the Sabbath of Christ without works, but faith alone.

And our works aren't needed, except to do good, to do the will of the Father. To find the lost sheep. To heal those that are broken. This is the spiritual application for salvation and the our purpose of sharing the Gospel that the Sabbath pictured in the OT.

teachings.title: Circumcision and the yoke of the law
teachings.summary: Galatians shows the problem is not the act of circumcision but seeking justification through it, which puts men under the law's yoke and makes the gospel of none effect.
teachings.text:
We see Paul's view that it's not the act of circumcision but the heart of those seeking justification with God through the act, and being placed in bondage under the yoke of the law. That false prophets crept in to mislead the early churches and by doing so make the Gospel to none effect of those who took heed of them. And so the demand of Titus to be circumcised prompted the council in Jerusalem, and the decision of James the half-brother of Jesus and the rest to make certain this heresy was warned against.

While in Timothy's case it was "nothing" as Paul says, for him to be circumcised simply to have entry to the Jews in the region to preach the Gospel.

Paul's epistles have his attitude regarding both his unwavering belief in the Gospel of faith and the need, as an Apostle to become all things to all people that they may know Jesus.

Hope this helps clear up the seeming contradiction between Paul's actions in those chapters in Acts.

teachings.title: Why Paul circumcised Timothy
teachings.summary: Paul refused circumcision for Titus because it was pressed as a condition of salvation, yet circumcised Timothy for access to the Jews, since circumcision is nothing when not made a means of justification.
teachings.text:
There is a lot going on here, in this chapter. Especially on the heels of 15, where we see the pillars of the church in Jerusalem issuing their judgment that Paul go to the Gentiles and their denouncing the adding of works to the faith that saved them. They agree at Paul's behest to write and visit the various churches, warning them against taking on the yoke of bondage to the carnal ordinances of the law, primarily circumcision. This crisis comes about by new Christians, confused in the faith by certain men crept in unawares, seeking to force Gentile Titus to be circumcised as part of salvation. Paul steadfastly refuses understanding the what they were attempting to do would subvert the Gospel, and James and the other apostles agree.

Yet here we see Paul circumcised Timothy, who being half-Gentile, but raised Jewish by his mother, would be hindered by the Jews in the region when giving the Gospel. And as Paul says in 1 Corinthians, in this case *Circumcision is nothing,* because it's not being put forth as a condition of justification before God.

We must look at the epistles to Corinth and especially the Galatians for more understanding, and so I think I will devote time to them today and tomorrow.

teachings.title: The promise was to Abraham's seed, which is Christ
teachings.summary: The promise to Abraham was made to his seed Christ and to all who are in Christ, the land promise was fulfilled under Joshua and kept conditionally under the Mosaic covenant, so Zionism wrongly gives the inheritance to unbelieving Jews.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 48** broadly captures the grandeur and love of God towards His holy land. This love is seen long before Israel as a nation enters in, or even exists. It was in the beginning, when God promised a land to Abraham.

**Genesis 12:1–3**
*Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.*

The promise to Abraham was both for the land, and the Christ. Long before the exodus. Long before the wandering. Before Isaac was ever born, the land that would become Israel, the province of Judah, the city of Jerusalem, in the mountains of Zion, was set apart for God.

The blessings and inheritance made to Abraham, who believed God and it was counted for righteousness, was made to him and his seed. Jesus Christ.

**Galatians 3:16**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.*

Zionism is a modern political ideology that takes the promise to Abraham, and rather than give the inheritance and blessing to Christ, and all who are in Christ, gives it to unbelieving, apostate Jews.

**Galatians 3:27–29**
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

The claim for the children of Israel to the land, by promise of God, was fulfilled in the time of Joshua.

**Joshua 21:43–45**
*And the LORD gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein. And the LORD gave them rest round about, according to all that he sware unto their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them; the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand. There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass.*

The promise to Abraham was unconditional. But the promise made to Moses by God in the wilderness, for His people to occupy His land, was conditional.

**Deuteronomy 28:63–64**
*And it shall come to pass, that as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you; so the LORD will rejoice over you to destroy you, and to bring you to nought; and ye shall be plucked from off the land whither thou goest to possess it. And the LORD shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.*

Many Christians today will say "God keeps His promises! The Jews deserve this land!" They place political Zionism and the ethnic ultranationalism of the modern Jewish state as being part of an unconditional and irrevocable covenant with the people by heritage and genealogy.

But the Bible is clear, that the covenant made in the wilderness was explicitly conditional, that what was given to the people through Moses could not, by their failure, disannul the promise made to Abraham and his singular seed.

**Galatians 3:17–18**
*And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect. For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.*

But the covenant made those 430 years after Abraham? It has faded away, replace by a better covenant with better promises, to all who are in Christ, regardless of their ethnicity or origin.

teachings.title: The inheritance belongs to all in Christ
teachings.summary: The land promise is fulfilled in the resurrection and the inheritance passes to all who have put on Christ, so Christians who give it away to modern Zionism for politics are like Esau selling his birthright.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 8:7–10**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people*

The promise to occupy the land will be fulfilled for the Old Testament believers, in the resurrection. The only "Zionism" that matters is Christ Jesus on His throne. The inheritance is passed to all who have put on Christ.

**Romans 8:14–17**
*For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together*.

This promise, the inheritance and blessings, is the heritage of all believers, from Adam and Abel, Seth and Noah, through every professing Christian today.

The spirit of Esau, who forsook his inheritance for a bowl of pottage, lives in Christians, who for political expediency seek to give it away.

**Hebrews 12:14–17**
*Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled; Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.*

This tearful repentance will be the case for many in the end times. Those who placed modern politics and bad theology above the joy unspeakable found in Jesus for all who believe, Jew or Gentile. Man or woman. Bond or free.

teachings.title: A godly seed: the promise was always Christ
teachings.summary: The godly seed God sought is Christ, the singular seed of Abraham, and Israel's marriage covenant ended when they slew their Husband.
teachings.text:
Malachi, the last prophet before the days of the coming of Christ, continues to preach the word of God against the Jews.

First Levi and her priests, then Judah and her foreign brides. Their iniquity and calling evil good and good evil.

Their table has become a snare.

Their adultery is to the covenant God made with their fathers, and to Him. And here, in Malachi 2:15, we see the reason behind the covenant, the Old Testament given to Moses in the wilderness. That He may seek a godly seed.

While some will say this is about Israel, it is, like God's promise to Abraham, seed singular. As of one.

**Galatians 3:16-17**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ. And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.*

The promise was always Christ.

*And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.*

This was always the gospel. This was always the promise. The good news.

And the fault for the first testament ending was with the people. The Lord hates putting away. And so in death, their marriage was ended, even the death of Christ.

The law says *The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead*.

They slew their Husband, and hung Him on a tree.

teachings.title: Circumcision of the heart is what matters
teachings.summary: Scripture moves from circumcision of the flesh to pleas for circumcised hearts until in the New Testament only circumcision of the heart counts, open to believing Gentiles.
teachings.text:
Looking back at **Ezekiel 44**, we find the giving of ordinances for the priests and the temple, beginning with the command that the East Gate, which the presence of the Lord would enter through, would remain shut and not be for any man to enter, but for the prince, or king, to enter via a porch entrance of the gate, a smaller door within it. That he would enter and sit before it to eat bread before the Lord, and go out the same.

Ezekiel is then taken to the North Gate, and falls to his knees when he sees the glory of the Lord filling the house of the Lord, the temple.

He is again instructed to see with his eyes and hear with his ears, that he may tell others. This command is repeatedly used in Ezekiel, and is found throughout scripture in other contexts as instructions for the righteous. For the saved. We are told to observe, hear and repeat to others.

Even to the rebellious. We are to preach His word and ways to the lost, and if they don't heed, like the man who ignores the warning trumpet, it is on them.

Here, God says to Israel, let this teaching *suffice you of all your abominations.* He is telling them what they need to do to get right.

God talks about the bringing in of strangers, foreigners (and their idols), who are not His people, into the house of the Lord, polluting it. Note, that He sets aside the allowance of non-Isralites who are either circumcised of the heart, or flesh. Who are saved believers or are assimilated into the nation.

The provision for the circumcision of the heart among strangers seems to be a broadening of the terms. In other places, there has been an appeal for the children of Israel to circumcise their hearts towards the Lord. Such as the appeal to the rebellious people in **Deuteronomy 10:6** *Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.* An appeal repeated several times, including

**Jeremiah 4:4**
*Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: lest my fury come forth like fire, and burn that none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.*

In the New Testament, it is only the circumcision of the heart that is welcome to the Lord.

**Romans 2:28-29**
*For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God*.

So, we see the progression. Hebrews after the flesh are circumcised, beginning with Abraham. In the wilderness, mostly in Deuteronomy and Leviticus, the circumcised of the flesh are asked to circumcise their hearts as well.

By the beginning of captivity, it is a plea to get saved, and avoid the coming destruction.

Here, in the midst of the captivity, when discussing an OT Temple that could be, it is included to count for Gentiles who believed.

In the New Testament, it becomes the only circumcision that matters.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple as what could have been
teachings.summary: Ezekiel's temple may be read as what could have been, since God with foreknowledge set conditional promises before Israel under the Mosaic covenant, which they failed to keep.
teachings.text:
Here in **Ezekiel 45**, the instructions for a temple and a time where there will be a priesthood of Zadok, Levites given land by cast lots for suburbs around the restored Temple. And sacrifices made for various offerings, the measure of which are given for "just balances," precise volumes, that nothing is cheated or anyone give more than another.

Similar to the existing Levitical laws, given unto Moses, the prophesied Temple in **Ezekiel 40-48** has similar Old Testament offerings and carnal ordinances, Sabbaths and holy days, done away with in the reformation of the New Testament.

We have looked at 4 main theories regarding this prophecy.; that it is symbolic and represents the church in Christ and Jesus our temple.

That it is literal, meant to be the design for the 2nd Temple Ezra will begin after captivity. That they fell short in grandeur and size.

That it is a future Temple, for the 3rd Temple leading up to the beginning of the Tribulation.

That it is a Temple in the millennial Kingdom, or in the eternal Kingdom.

All these theories have problems that make them more and more unlikely to be true. The secret things are His and we see through a glass darkly, but surely there's a purpose and a reason for Ezekiel to cap off his end times prophecies, that extend back to chapter 33. That the restoration promised also applies to the prophecy of the Temple.

Which brings us to another theory which I truthfully hadn't considered before. The interpretation of "what could have been."

First, we must acknowledge that God knows the end from the beginning, and the invisible things of what hasn't happened yet.

**Isaiah 46:9-10**
*Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.*

God knows our decisions before we make them, but also allows us the free will to make them, and gives constant appeals to repentance, and encourages us to choose His ways and seek His paths.

The Lord gave the covenant to Israel through Moses with this clear understanding.

**Deuteronomy 30:15-20**
*See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it. But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.*

God made these conditional promises to Israel as a nation, with the foreknowledge that they would fail. Unlike the Abrahamic and Davidic covenants, which were mostly unconditional (depending on the men themselves to believe God, and have it counted for righteousness), the Mosaic covenant, with the commandments and Levitical laws, depended on the people to keep up their end in order to obtain the Kingdom and the promises and the blessings that would come if they would. And in His grace, multiple opportunities for restitution if they failed.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple: the offer that will never be
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 40-48 describes a kingdom God graciously offered Israel if they repented, which will now never be because they rejected Christ.
teachings.text:
All this to say that the 5th theory of Ezekiel's Temple is that it is a picture of a promise for an end-times that will now never be. That God was promising the Jews in captivity a chance to make things right. That by His grace and mercy and longsuffering, He was telling them of the glory of the Kingdom of God that He had in mind for them IF they turned back and were faithful.

An alternate ending of things that, though He knew wouldn't come, God was graciously offering Israel, one last time.

And so Jesus came not to judge the world, which He would have had they listened, but to offer salvation.

**John 12:47**
*And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.*

God continued to see His will done, by other means. Because, despite the Calvinist protests, we are given free will, yet our God is not weak and beggarly as Calvin's having to micromanage everything to reach a conclusion He desires. The Lord can let all creation do as all creatures will, and regardless of our choices, still will His Kingdom come.

And so, Ezekiel's Temple will never be. It was an offer that isn't. Not because of a flaw with God, but with the people.

An alternate universe, where **Ezekiel 40-48** serves as **Revelation**. It's the most glaring example of what could have been in the Old Testament end-times prophecy. An achievable promise, rejected by those it was promised to.

teachings.title: The new heart promise fulfilled in Christ, not 1948
teachings.summary: The promise of a new heart and new covenant in Ezekiel 36 is fulfilled in Christ for the Israel of God, not in the UN-created state of unbelieving Jews.
teachings.text:
The second half of **Ezekiel 36** drifts into end times prophecy. A new promise, which we have seen made elsewhere, where He will give a new heart, and a new spirit within the people, and His Spirit within, and cause us by the law in our hearts to walk in His statutes, and to keep His commandments. To dwell in the land of the fathers. *And ye shall be My people, and I will be your God*.

**Jeremiah 31:31-34**
*Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they brake, although I was an husband unto them, saith the Lord: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the Lord, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people. And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the Lord: for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.*

**Hebrews 10:16-17**
*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

This promise is fulfilled in Christ.

This is not fulfilled by the UN creating the modern state of Israel. They have not gotten a new heart. They have not accepted Christ. Their desolation has not become like the garden of Eden. They are not ashamed and confounded, remembering their sin, loathing themselves for their iniquity.

This promise of restoration is done to the Israel of God, both OT and NT believers, in the end times.

 Not unbelieving Jews today.

teachings.title: We have Abraham to our father
teachings.summary: The claim that the Jews inherit the land as Abraham's many children is the false basis of Zionism, since the promises were always conditional on obedience to God's covenant.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 33** concludes, the destruction of Jerusalem has happened. One who escaped comes to the prophet in the evening and tells him, but the hand of God keeps Ezekiel from responding until the morning came, and he was no longer struck dumb. And he receives the word of God.

The Lord says that those from the wastes and wilderness of Judah, who escaped out of the desolation of Jerusalem speak, saying that because Abraham was one, and was promised land, that they being many deserve the inheritance.

This is the argument made by Jews today. The basis of Zionism. The false doctrine that because they are children of the law, and many, the promise of the land given Abraham should apply even more so to them.

**Matthew 3:9**
*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

The promises and inheritance was never given a people because of who they were. But by the condition of what they did. A condition repeatedly given.

**Exodus 19:5**
*Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine*

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

The word of the Lord upon Ezekiel stresses these same points. They are filled with violence and Idolatry and adultery and abominations.

For this, God says He will lay the land most desolate because of their abominations. Then they shall know He is the Lord.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: Jerusalem as dross
teachings.summary: Jerusalem broke the old covenant through idolatry, false prophets and oppressing the poor, despised God's longsuffering, and was judged and cast out like dross, which is why a new covenant was needed.
teachings.text:
We see here in the preaching against Jerusalem, where the Lord demands the prophet tell the Jews of their abominations and His judgment, that much of it mirrors those things given to Moses in the wilderness. The things God proclaimed should be dealt with by death. That the blood be upon the wicked and not on the people in the land.

But the children of Israel failed to uphold their end of the covenant and now faced the promised judgment.

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
